system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Our Buyer Negotiation Playbook, the Seller Update, and the Seller Disclosure Letter dated 22 September 2026. Both Seller documents are counterparty material. Nothing in them is agreed.

---

## 1. Framing points

1. **"Key Negotiated Positions" is the Seller's label.** It does not make any position agreed. We should not treat the cover note's "fair and balanced package" or the reference to "agreed price mechanics" as agreement on anything (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3).
2. **The Disclosure Letter is more candid than the Update, and it undercuts it.** On Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar, the Letter confirms that the protections or evidence we need are missing, while the Update calls the same matters "addressed", "adequate" or "not material". We should use the Seller's own Letter in the mark-up.
3. **The Letter is stale.** It speaks as at 22 September 2026, and today is 6 November 2026. Every factual item (Bluefen, Riverlark balance, DD-006 investigation, Ironquay payment) needs a refreshed, dated update. We should not rely on the September position as current.
4. **The Update has hidden override clauses.** Clause 12.3/13 ("any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise") and clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 ("all Claims of any nature") would sweep Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, covenant, payment and fraud claims into the general regime. This departs from the playbook in a structural way, beyond any single number.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability architecture

| # | Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment and pushback |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a fallback only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft | **Reject. Hold 25%.** The 20% figure matches our fallback, but that does not clear it. No authority has been given. We must not signal that 20% is acceptable. If the team wants to concede, escalate to Amelia Frost in writing, identifying this draft, before any movement. |
| 2 | **De minimis / basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k basket; excess only | AUD 5k; AUD 50k; first dollar once exceeded | **Reject all three elements.** The de minimis is 5x ours and the basket is 5x ours. The "excess only" (deductible) structure removes the first AUD 250k of every claim in aggregate. Together these could exclude a meaningful slice of real loss. Restore 5k / 50k / tipping basket. |
| 3 | **General claims period (cl 12.3)** | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months only with Amelia Frost approval (none) | **Reject. Hold 24 months.** |
| 4 | **"Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | Proposed | Categories kept separate; no hidden general-regime override | **Delete.** It reverses the burden, so every carve-out must be drafted perfectly or the general limits apply by default. Replace it with an express statement that the general limits apply **only** to general Warranty Claims. |
| 5 | **Fundamental / Title** | Same caps and time limits as general "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | **Reject outright.** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay for. Capping them at 20% of price is not an administrative point. |
| 6 | **Limitations / exclusive remedy / non-reliance (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)** apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Proposed | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Not waivable | **Reject. Insert a full fraud carve-out.** As drafted, there is no fraud exception at all. This is non-negotiable under the playbook, and no one on our side can trade it. Separately, specific indemnities, covenants, Tax, IP and payment obligations must sit outside the general exclusive-remedy and limitation provisions. |
| 7 | **Tax / IP** | "Settled under the general regime" | OPEN. No unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed | **Reject the characterisation.** Tax and IP are not settled. State in our mark-up that both remain open and are to be dealt with in separate provisions. Do not concede them into the general regime, and do not overclaim (we have not agreed unlimited liability either). |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**8. General disclosure (Schedule 7; Letter 1.1–1.2).** The Seller discloses the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 and everything "referred to" in it), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- **Departure:** The playbook requires specific fair disclosure and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Pushback:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2. The "without limiting any specific disclosure" wording in 1.2 does not cure the problem, because the general disclosure still qualifies every warranty. Only matters fairly disclosed in the Letter with enough detail to identify their nature and scope should qualify the warranties.
- Letter 1.4 (no admission) is broadly acceptable as a non-admission statement. It must not operate to narrow or deny the disclosed facts.

**9. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** "No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Departure:** This is a blanket exclusion covering imputed adviser knowledge and constructive knowledge ("discoverable"). It combines with the general disclosure to create a double bar.
- **Pushback:** Delete. If any qualifier survives, it must:
  - be limited to actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry (Seller-side knowledge for Seller-qualified warranties);
  - not impute knowledge of our advisers or deem knowledge from the data room or public records; and
  - never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### C. Transaction-specific matters

**10. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; Letter item 2).**
- The facts matter here. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, roughly 30%. There is a change-control consent clause (11.2) with conditions (11.3). The Letter confirms that, as at 22 September, there was **no final written consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied.**
- The Update says the consent is "addressed", but it proposes only reasonable endeavours plus deemed satisfaction "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent". That would let a consent that is conditional, qualified or still subject to unsatisfied 11.3 conditions count as satisfied.
- **Pushback:** Make it a Completion condition that cannot be waived except by the Buyer. It should require:
  - an effective, unconditional (or Buyer-approved conditional) written consent; and
  - evidence that all clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.

  Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of this size. Ask for the current status, since the September position is six weeks old.

**11. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; Letter item 3).**
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. There is change-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2). The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is in the data room. The Seller offers only "a release to be provided following Completion", with no undertaking or mechanism.
- **Departure:** The playbook requires a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval, and neither is present.
- **Pushback:**
  - Require a dated payout letter from Riverlark. "Approximately AUD 3.2m" is not a payout figure.
  - Require direct payment to Riverlark from Completion funds, counted as Debt in the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.
  - Require delivery at Completion of executed releases and PPSR discharge (or Riverlark's binding undertaking to discharge on receipt, in agreed form).
  - Confirm whether the Riverlark security includes any share mortgage or security over the Sale Shares. If it does, this is also a Title issue (see item 16).
  - The 8.1 change-control clause means Completion itself may trigger default. That is another reason repayment must happen at Completion.

**12. Employee bonuses (Letter item 5; funds flow note).**
- DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000. The Letter confirms they do **not** appear in the funds flow and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- The Update says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but does not itemise them. If the Company pays them after Completion, the Buyer bears the cost economically. This is the "silent exclusion" the playbook warns against.
- **Pushback:** Either (a) a specific funds-flow line item treating AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as Debt / a price deduction, paid through payroll, or (b) express Seller funding with an indemnity covering the bonuses and on-costs. Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost treatment. We should not assume a figure for on-costs. Also confirm how the continued-employment conditions interact with Completion timing.

**13. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; Letter item 4).**
- DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. The Letter itself notes this is not independent verification of non-payment. There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- The Seller says the existing indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, is "adequate".
- **Pushback:** Broaden the indemnity to cover:
  - loss from any failure of the Company to own, or obtain transfer of, the SOW3 Project Materials;
  - Ironquay claims; and
  - third-party IP claims relating to those materials.

  Preserve the SOW3 cure (payment of outstanding fees and delivery of a confirmatory assignment). Ideally obtain both before Completion. We should not treat the AUD 180,000 as verified in either direction. Ask for the Ironquay account statement and bank records. Keep the indemnity outside the general cap and basket.

**14. DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; Letter item 6).**
- A download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Access, scope and any notification requirement are all unestablished. The investigation is preliminary.
- The Seller's statement that the matter "is not expected to be material" is an assertion, not a finding.
- **Our position:** Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss in either direction. Equally, we do not accept "not material".
- **Pushback:** Covenants requiring the Seller and Company to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete and document the investigation, including the assessment of whether notification is required;
  - provide regular written updates and the final findings before Completion; and
  - not settle, notify or make admissions without Buyer consultation.

  Seek a specific warranty or indemnity for loss arising from the incident, sitting outside the general regime. Do not put a number on it or assert a breach.

**15. Sandbar renewals (Letter item 8).**
- Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total) appear across DD-008 and DD-011, to be read together. The Seller calls them "ordinary-course operating costs". The Letter itself says it does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Pushback:** Assess before deciding treatment. Request the contracts, renewal dates, termination rights and accrual status, and why the three were timed together. We should not classify them automatically as Debt or seek a price deduction, and we should not accept the "ordinary course" label without that information.

**16. Title (Letter item 10).**
- The only title evidence is the Company's own share register (DD-012). The Letter concedes this is merely "the source relied on" and that we have not verified it.
- **Pushback:** Require independent evidence:
  - an ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share certificates;
  - a PPSR and encumbrance search over the Sale Shares and the Seller;
  - Seller board approval and authority to sell; and
  - confirmation of no options, rights or other claims over the shares.

  Title warranties stay in the Fundamental regime (item 5).

**17. Lower-priority items (Letter items 7 and 9).**
- **Office lease (DD-007):** There is a notification obligation. Confirm the timing and who gives the notice, and make giving it a Seller covenant.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** There is an assignment restriction. The Seller says it is not triggered by a share sale. We should verify this by reading the full contract, including any change-of-control or "deemed assignment" provisions, rather than relying on the Letter's description.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Hold the playbook baseline on all limitation terms.** That means a 25% / AUD 6.0m cap, AUD 5k / AUD 50k tipping basket, and 24 months. Do not concede 20% or 18 months. Both need Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none exists. Escalate only if the team decides to move.
2. **Delete the general-regime override** in cl 12.3/13, and narrow cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 so they apply only to general Warranty Claims.
3. **Insert a full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. This is non-negotiable.
4. **Reinstate a separate Fundamental/Title regime** with a 100% cap and at least 6 years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. **Record Tax and IP as OPEN** in separate provisions. Reject "settled under the general regime".
6. **Delete general disclosure** (Letter 1.1–1.2) and require specific fair disclosure.
7. **Delete the buyer-knowledge bar** (cl 8.3). Any fallback should be limited to named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, with no application to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
8. **Bluefen:** make an effective consent plus evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied a Completion condition. Reject reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery.
9. **Riverlark:** require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and releases at Completion. Reject the unsecured post-Completion release. Check for any share security.
10. **Bonuses:** require a funds-flow line item or Seller funding for AUD 420,000 plus all on-costs. Obtain the Seller's on-cost confirmation.
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity beyond the SOW3 payment, preserve the SOW3 cure, and verify payment status independently.
12. **DD-006:** require preservation, investigation, update covenants and a specific protection. Take no position on breach, notification or quantum either way.
13. **Sandbar:** request information and assess. No automatic Debt or price treatment.
14. **Title:** require ASIC, PPSR, certificates and authority evidence beyond DD-012.
15. **Process:** ask for a refreshed Disclosure Letter dated close to signing, since the 22 September facts are stale. In our cover note, state that no position in the Seller Update is agreed.

**Suggested next step:** I can turn this into a marked-up issues list or response cover note to the Seller's counsel.
=== END ADVICE ===
